prompt.context_jp: 検査室の空気___張り詰めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 検査室の空気___張り詰めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that best fits the opening scene description.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is setting the scene with 空気 as the topic frame: 'as for the air in the room, it was tense.' は presents it as the backdrop against which the scene unfolds.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sudden new information, as if we just noticed the tension; here the narrator is framing the atmosphere, not reporting a discovery.

contrast_examples.jp: 空気は張り詰めていた。
contrast_examples.en: The air was tense (setting the scene).

contrast_examples.jp: 急に空気が張り詰めた。
contrast_examples.en: Suddenly the air grew tense (new event).

prompt.context_jp: 人と向き合うことは苦手でも、画像の前でだけ___彼の背筋は迷わない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 画像の前でだけ___彼の背筋は迷わない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that captures the contrast with his social awkwardness.

feedback.correct_en: は after だけ sharpens the contrast: he struggles with people, but only in front of images is he confident. This は explicitly pits one situation against another.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would merely report a fact without the contrastive bite the narrator is building here.

contrast_examples.en: Here, at least, I won't lose (contrast).

prompt.context_jp: 隣に腰を下ろした志朗の膝には、握りしめられた拳___置かれている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 握りしめられた拳___置かれている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces this detail to the reader.

feedback.correct_en: The clenched fist is new information the narrator is pointing out for the first time — a classic existential 'there is X' structure takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the fist was already an established topic, which it isn't. を doesn't fit with the intransitive 置かれている.

contrast_examples.en: There is a book on the desk (new info).

contrast_examples.jp: その本は机の上にある。
contrast_examples.en: That book (known) is on the desk.

prompt.context_jp: 真貴の顔色___白く、蛍光灯の光さえ息を潜めているようだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 真貴の顔色___白く…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames Maki's complexion as the subject of description.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator makes 真貴の顔色 the topic and describes its state — a stative characterization, not a sudden discovery, so は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like we just noticed her paleness as breaking news; here the narrator is quietly describing the ongoing scene.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女の顔色は青かった。
彼女の顔色が急に変わった。

prompt.context_jp: 「右の乳房に2センチを超える ギザギザのしこり___あります」
prompt.prompt_jp: 右の乳房に…ギザギザのしこり___あります。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Igarashi uses when first presenting the finding.

feedback.correct_en: He is announcing the existence of the lump for the first time — brand-new information in an ある-sentence, which takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the lump was already a known topic; he is introducing it to the patient.

contrast_examples.jp: ここにしこりがあります。
contrast_examples.en: There is a lump here (first disclosure).

contrast_examples.jp: そのしこりは2センチです。

prompt.context_jp: 「悪性の腫瘍___ギザギザで…顔つきが悪いというんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 悪性の腫瘍___ギザギザで…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle used when explaining a general property of malignant tumors.

feedback.correct_en: A generic/categorical statement — 'malignant tumors (as a class) are jagged' — takes は to mark the kind being characterized.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would single out a particular tumor as new information, which doesn't fit the general explanation he is giving.

prompt.context_jp: 「確かに 蛭田さんのしこりは 顔つき___よくありません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 蛭田さんのしこりは 顔つき___よくありません。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the inner subject in this topic-comment structure.

feedback.correct_en: This is a classic double-subject pattern: X は Y が Z. しこり is the topic (は), and 顔つき is the inner subject whose quality is being described, so が.
feedback.incorrect_en: Using は again would create two competing topics in one clause and sounds unnatural; を doesn't fit with the adjectival predicate.

contrast_examples.en: Elephants have long noses (topic は + inner subject が).

contrast_examples.jp: このしこりは形が悪い。
contrast_examples.en: This lump has a bad shape.

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐の指先___、悪性を思わせる輪郭の内側にそっと触れた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 五十嵐の指先___…そっと触れた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this cinematic descriptive sentence.

feedback.correct_en: A narrative action sentence describing what happens in the scene — the fingertips are the acting subject, not an established topic, so が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn this into a comment about his fingertips as a theme; the narrator is instead showing a single visual action.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の手はいつも震えている。

prompt.context_jp: だが彼の視線___、その奥に隠れた別の輪郭を追っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: だが彼の視線___、その奥に隠れた別の輪郭を追っている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. Note the preceding sentence described his fingertips.

feedback.correct_en: だが signals contrast: his fingers touched one outline, but his gaze (は) is tracking another. は highlights the shift of focus between the two.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply report a new fact without the contrastive link to the previous sentence that だが sets up.

contrast_examples.jp: 手は止まったが、目は動いていた。
contrast_examples.en: His hand stopped, but his eyes kept moving (contrast).

prompt.context_jp: 五十嵐の声___静かで、しかし確かな重みを帯びていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 五十嵐の声___静かで…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle framing his voice as the subject of the description.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is characterizing his voice — a stative description with two balanced qualities (quiet, but weighty). Characterizations of a known entity use は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make his voice sound like a new discovery in the scene rather than a described attribute.

prompt.context_jp: 重い沈黙の後、真貴の睫毛に涙___滲んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 真貴の睫毛に涙___滲んだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the emotional moment of tears appearing.

feedback.correct_en: Tears welling up is a sudden, perceivable event — the kind of spontaneous appearance が naturally marks.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat tears as an already-known topic; here they appear for the first time as a dramatic beat.

prompt.context_jp: 技師である五十嵐が説明を担う光景に、彼女___言葉を失っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女___言葉を失っている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the continuing topic 'she (Amakasu).'

feedback.correct_en: Amakasu has already been introduced in the previous sentence (甘春杏). As a continuing topic described with a state, 彼女 takes は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce her as new information, which clashes with the fact that she was just named.

prompt.context_jp: 机の上に投げ出された写真の束___、二人の間の距離をいっそう際立たせている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 写真の束___、二人の間の距離を…際立たせている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the pile of photos as it's introduced into the scene.

feedback.correct_en: The stack of photos is a newly introduced visual element that the narrator spotlights — it takes が as the fresh subject of the sentence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the photos were an established topic; they are first named in this very sentence as scenery.

contrast_examples.jp: 机の上に手紙があった。
contrast_examples.en: A letter was on the desk (new scene element).

prompt.context_jp: 「以前の写真には しこり___ はっきり写っていました。再検査したところで 結果は変わらないはずです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 以前の写真には しこり___ はっきり写っていました。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Amakasu uses to emphasize the lump against the re-exam issue.

feedback.correct_en: Amakasu is building a contrastive argument: the lump WAS clearly there in the earlier scan (so a re-exam shouldn't change anything). は foregrounds しこり as the point of contention.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would merely report the lump's presence neutrally; the surrounding reproach needs contrastive は to land.

contrast_examples.jp: 前の写真にはしこりははっきり写っていた。
contrast_examples.en: In the earlier scan, the lump WAS clearly visible (contrastive).

contrast_examples.jp: 前の写真にしこりが写っていた。
contrast_examples.en: A lump was visible in the earlier scan (plain report).

prompt.context_jp: 「患者を救うっていう夢___ 叶えてるじゃない」
prompt.prompt_jp: 患者を救うっていう夢___ 叶えてるじゃない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Maki uses when telling Shiro about his dream.

feedback.correct_en: The dream is the topic she's commenting on — 'as for that dream, you ARE living it.' は sets it up as the theme being affirmed.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would need an active verb (夢を叶えている). が would awkwardly reintroduce the dream as new info rather than comment on it.

contrast_examples.en: Your dream is being realized (comment on topic).

prompt.context_jp: 「私たちを救ってくれた___ 技師さんだよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私たちを救ってくれた___ 技師さんだよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this cleft-style identification.

feedback.correct_en: This is a cleft: 'The one who saved us was the technician.' The nominalized clause のは sets up the presupposition, and the predicate identifies the answer.
feedback.incorrect_en: のが would be used when the whole event is new to perception (e.g., 'I saw the technician save us'); here Maki is identifying WHO did the saving, which calls for のは.

contrast_examples.jp: 助けてくれたのは彼だ。
contrast_examples.en: The one who helped me was him (cleft identification).

prompt.context_jp: 「時間がかかってしまい ___ 、角度を変えて追加撮影をする 必要があったんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 時間がかかってしまい ___ 。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the apology appropriate for a professional addressing a patient.

choices.text: 申し訳ありませんでした

feedback.correct_en: In a clinical setting speaking to a patient, 申し訳ありませんでした is the expected formal apology for a delay.
feedback.incorrect_en: ごめん and 悪いね are casual and would sound inappropriately familiar in a hospital examination room.

contrast_examples.jp: お待たせして申し訳ありません。
contrast_examples.en: I'm sorry to keep you waiting (polite).

prompt.context_jp: 「その腫瘍の見た目を ___ と表現します」
prompt.prompt_jp: その腫瘍の見た目を ___ と表現します。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the radiology term Igarashi uses for a tumor's appearance.

feedback.correct_en: 顔つき ('visage/features') is the specific term radiologists use for how a lesion looks on imaging — the whole scene builds on this metaphor.
feedback.incorrect_en: 表情 means facial expression (requires animacy), and 様子 is too vague — neither carries the clinical metaphor the chapter title 違う顔 plays on.

contrast_examples.en: The tumor's visage is bad (radiology term).

prompt.context_jp: 彼は写真を指し示しながら、断定を ___ 言い回しを慎重に選んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 断定を ___ 言い回しを慎重に選んだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that captures Igarashi's careful hedging.

feedback.correct_en: 断定を避ける ('to avoid making definitive statements') is exactly the collocation for his careful, non-doctor positioning here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 決める or 強める would suggest the opposite — committing to or strengthening a diagnosis — which contradicts his stance.

contrast_examples.en: He avoided making a definitive claim.

prompt.context_jp: 「僕は 医者ではないので ___ をすることはできません」
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕は 医者ではないので ___ をすることはできません。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose what Igarashi says he cannot do as a non-doctor.

feedback.correct_en: 断言をする = 'to state definitively.' He is signaling he can't officially declare a diagnosis because he isn't a doctor.
feedback.incorrect_en: 発言 just means 'remark,' and 宣言 is a formal public declaration (like a treaty) — neither fits a medical hedge.

prompt.context_jp: 「あんな ___ 大腿骨頸部骨折に気付けるなんて」
prompt.prompt_jp: あんな ___ 大腿骨頸部骨折に気付けるなんて。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adjective describing how hard the fracture was to spot.

feedback.correct_en: The point of Hirose's admiration is that the fracture was hard to detect — 分かりづらい ('hard to make out') fits the praise.
feedback.incorrect_en: 分かりやすい and 見やすい mean the opposite (easy to see), which would make the praise meaningless.

prompt.context_jp: 「___ じゃねえか」(軒下が差し入れを受け取って)
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ じゃねえか。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom Nokishita uses to say 'how thoughtful of you.'

feedback.correct_en: 気が利く means 'attentive/thoughtful.' Nokishita is gruffly complimenting Hirose for bringing him something.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気が重い = feeling down; 気が短い = short-tempered. Neither makes sense as a compliment.

prompt.context_jp: 医師と技師の職掌をめぐる倫理の線引きを、彼女は ___ わけにはいかない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女は ___ わけにはいかない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that means 'cannot overlook.'

feedback.correct_en: 看過する means 'to overlook/let slide.' Combined with わけにはいかない, it conveys 'she cannot let this pass.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 看病する = to nurse the sick; 観察する = to observe neutrally. Neither matches 'turn a blind eye.'

prompt.context_jp: 「まあ 性格は ___ けどね」(軒下について)
prompt.prompt_jp: 性格は ___ けどね。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the colorful phrase describing Nokishita's twisted personality.

feedback.correct_en: ひん曲がってる ('all twisted/warped') is slangy/colloquial and fits the roast-session tone about Nokishita's prickly personality.
feedback.incorrect_en: まっすぐな (straightforward) and やさしい (kind) would be compliments, not the complaints that follow (ロリコン、足が臭い…).

contrast_examples.jp: 性格がひん曲がっている。

prompt.context_jp: Igarashi is first informing Hiruta about the finding in her scan.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural for a radiologist's first disclosure?

choices.text: 右の乳房に2センチを超えるギザギザのしこりがあります。
右の乳房に2センチを超えるギザギザのしこりはあります。

feedback.correct_en: Introducing a newly discovered lump uses the existential ある-pattern with が. This matches the story's actual line.
feedback.incorrect_en: Version B with は would imply the lump was an already-known topic and oddly suggest contrast ('the lump IS there, but...'), which is not what he's conveying.

contrast_examples.jp: ここにしこりがあります。
contrast_examples.en: There is a lump here (first disclosure).

contrast_examples.jp: しこりはあるが、小さい。
contrast_examples.en: The lump IS there, but small (contrast).

prompt.context_jp: Igarashi evaluating the appearance of the lump on the mammogram.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version uses the radiology metaphor correctly?

choices.text: 蛭田さんのしこりは顔つきがよくありません。
蛭田さんのしこりは表情がよくありません。

feedback.correct_en: 顔つき is the established radiology metaphor for how a lesion 'looks' — it anchors the whole 違う顔 motif of this chapter.
feedback.incorrect_en: 表情 implies facial expression and requires an animate face; applied to a lump, it sounds wrong.

prompt.context_jp: Igarashi, hedging as a technician (not a doctor), tells Amakasu his reading.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for his professional hedge?

choices.text: 心配はないと思います。

feedback.correct_en: In a clinical, slightly tense exchange with a doctor, polite ~と思います hedges the opinion appropriately.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心配しないよ is casual self-reassurance (and grammatically wrong for conveying 'there's nothing to worry about'); it clashes with the workplace register.

contrast_examples.jp: 心配はないと思います。
contrast_examples.en: I don't think there's cause for worry (polite opinion).

prompt.context_jp: Maki tells Shiro who actually saved them.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version naturally identifies the savior?

choices.text: 私たちを救ってくれたのは技師さんだよ。
私たちを救ってくれた技師さんはだよ。

feedback.correct_en: The cleft [verb clause] + のは + [identification] + だ is the natural way to say 'the one who X was Y.'
feedback.incorrect_en: Option B is ungrammatical — は can't attach directly to a noun followed by だ in that position.

contrast_examples.en: The one who helped was him.

prompt.context_jp: Igarashi, flustered, asks Nokishita for advice at the bar.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural in this bar conversation with a senior colleague?

choices.text: 軒下さん、僕どうすればいいと思います？
軒下さん、僕どうすればいいと思いますか？

feedback.correct_en: In casual spoken Japanese, dropping か and relying on rising intonation after 思います sounds more natural and matches Igarashi's half-polite bar-talk register.
feedback.incorrect_en: Adding か isn't wrong, but feels stiffer than how Igarashi actually speaks here with Nokishita over drinks.

contrast_examples.en: What do you think? (polite but casual tone)
